action: Update n8n to 2.45.5, 2.46.1 or 3.0.1 or later, depending on your release line. Read GitHub advisory GHSA-426f-xmcv-g8pg linked from the Cyber Centre notice.
exec: Automation platforms hold credentials for many other systems, so an account-hijack flaw in one widens exposure; an update is available.
plain: Canada's cyber agency told organisations using n8n, a tool that connects apps and automates tasks, to update it. A flaw in how it links outside accounts could let someone hijack a connected account.

key_findings: Affected: n8n before 2.45.5, before 2.46.1 and before 3.0.1.
The linked GitHub advisory GHSA-426f-xmcv-g8pg is titled as an OAuth account hijack in the end-user credential connect flow through an unauthenticated callback.
The Cyber Centre page names no CVE identifiers.
The advisory makes no statement about exploitation.
recommendations: Review the GitHub advisory and the n8n security overview linked from the advisory.
Apply the necessary updates as they become available.

summary: Cyber Centre advisory AV26-1160 says the n8n workflow automation platform is affected before versions 2.45.5, 2.46.1 and 3.0.1. It links to a GitHub advisory describing an OAuth account hijack in the end-user credential connect flow, made possible by a callback that does not require authentication. The Cyber Centre page names no CVE and does not say whether the flaw is being exploited.
title: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security issues n8n advisory AV26-1160 over OAuth account hijack flaw

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Canadian Centre for Cyber Security document.
